改好了，08:02 准时开工。这就叫——**闹钟一响，积分自己长脚跑进兜里**。😎

## 改了什么

| 项 | 原来 | 现在 |
|---|---|---|
| 主签时间 | 00:05（半夜鸡叫） | **08:02**（人醒它也醒） |
| 补签兜底 | 01/05/09/13/17/21 点 | **12:02 / 16:02 / 20:02** |

兜底轮次特意挪到主签之后 —— 08:02 那次要是因为关机、断网、网络没睡醒跑砸了，后面三趟会先查状态、**没签就补**，连签链条不断。Buddy 出门旅行带回的礼物也能顺手领回来，不至于压到第二天。

## 现行 crontab（`crontab -l` 实拍）

```bash
# 每天 08:02 签到 + 成长中心（主签）
2 8 * * * /usr/bin/python3 .../signin.py silent >> .../cron.log 2>&1

# 补签兜底 + 成长中心轮询：12/16/20 点
2 12,16,20 * * * WORKBUDDY_SIGNIN_LOG=.../signin-poll.log /usr/bin/python3 .../signin.py silent-poll >> .../cron.log 2>&1
```

## 验证结果

- 模拟 cron 空环境（`env -i`）跑两条命令：**exit=0，双通过**
- cron 守护进程在跑：root 起的 `/usr/sbin/cron -f`，状态 active
- 日志末条：今日已签过 · 连续 3 天 · 累计 300 积分 · Buddy 咖啡馆旅行中

```dsh-ui
{"title":"签到时间表 · 已改 08:02","gap":12,"items":[{"type":"hero","value":"08:02","label":"每日主签时间","tone":"success"},{"type":"timeline","items":[{"title":"08:02 · 主签","desc":"silent：签到 + 成长中心全套，结果写 signin.log"},{"title":"12:02 · 兜底","desc":"silent-poll：漏签自动补 + 领 Buddy 旅行礼物"},{"title":"16:02 · 兜底","desc":"同上，空跑不写日志，不打扰"},{"title":"20:02 · 兜底","desc":"当天最后一次补签机会，关机错过的日子补不了，但这趟能救开机晚的情况"}]},{"type":"callout","tone":"success","title":"改完已实测","content":"crontab 已重新载入，两条命令在模拟 cron 空环境下退出码均为 0。改时间只需编辑 workbuddy-auto-signin/crontab.workbuddy 后跑 crontab crontab.workbuddy。"}]}
```

- `genui`: GenUI dsh-ui component/schema reference. Preserve conversation language for all user-visible text.
- `jimeng-video-pipeline`: 即梦画布 CLI 端到端竖屏短视频生产流水线（分段脚本 → 积分报价 → 逐段生成 → 合并 → 音频层（换声/BGM/音效）→ 合规字幕）。当用户要做 30 秒级竖屏短视频、需要分段生成再合并、要给成片加中文字幕与合规字幕、或需要换声/配 BGM/加音效时使用。依赖已安装的 dreamina-canvas CLI 与 dsh-ffmpeg；音频环节依赖 dsh-audiogen。
- `jimeng-video-prompts`: Use when generating JiMeng AI video prompts.

entries.name: dsh-audiogen-voice-management

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Managed `$DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. An unset variable expands to an empty string, so guard variables in such paths with `${VAR:?}`. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap; on expiry the command moves to the background as a job instead of being killed.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact command the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact command needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

max_goal_rounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer limit on automatic continuation rounds.

Success means queued, not sent; do not claim the user has received the file.

path.description: Absolute path, or a path relative to the current workspace.

tools.name: ffmpeg_adjust
tools.description: 调整媒体：变速（speed 倍率，>1 加速 <1 减速，音视频同步变速）、音量（volume 倍数如 1.5 或分贝如 -3dB）、静音（mute）、顺时针旋转（rotate 90/180/270，竖横屏互转）。可组合使用。只静音/调音量时视频走流拷贝（快）；变速/旋转会重编码。四个操作至少给一个。

speed.description: 倍速 0.1-100：2 为两倍速，0.5 为半速（可选）。

volume.description: 音量：倍数如 1.5 / 0.6，或分贝如 -3dB / +2dB（可选）。

output.description: 输出路径（可选，默认输入同目录加 .adjust 后缀）。

tools.name: ffmpeg_concat
tools.description: 拼接多个视频片段。默认要求编码一致（流拷贝，秒级完成）；reencode=true 时统一重编码拼接（慢；先 probe 各输入，任一输入无音轨就按纯视频拼接，避免音轨绑定失败）。inputs 为 2-20 个文件路径。

inputs.description: 输入文件路径数组（2-20 个，必填）。

output.description: 输出路径（可选，默认第一个输入同目录加 .concat 后缀）。

reencode.description: 是否统一重编码拼接（默认 false=流拷贝）。

tools.name: ffmpeg_cut
tools.description: 剪辑视频片段。默认流拷贝（极快、关键帧对齐）；reencode=true 时精确到帧重编码（慢）。start 为起始时间（秒或 HH:MM:SS.mmm，默认 0）；end 与 duration 至少给一个（end 优先）。输出默认放在输入同目录，同名自动加序号。

start.description: 起始时间（秒或 HH:MM:SS.mmm，默认 0）。

end.description: 结束时间；与 duration 至少给一个。

duration.description: 片段时长；与 end 至少给一个。

output.description: 输出路径（可选，默认输入同目录加 .cut 后缀）。

reencode.description: 是否精确重编码（默认 false=流拷贝）。

tools.description: 转码输出。预设：bilibili-1080p（H.264+AAC，码率上限 6000k，faststart，B 站推荐）、bilibili-4k（上限 20000k）、vertical-1080p（竖屏 1080x1920）、web-720p（轻量）。可选覆盖 crf（0-51）、fps、scale（如 1920:1080）。

preset.description: 预设档位：bilibili-1080p / bilibili-4k / vertical-1080p / web-720p（默认 bilibili-1080p）。

output.description: 输出路径（可选，默认输入同目录加 .encoded 后缀）。

tools.name: ffmpeg_extract
tools.description: 提取媒体成分。what=audio 提取音轨（默认 .m4a：AAC 流拷贝，非 AAC 自动回退转码为 AAC）；what=frames 按 fps 抽帧序列（输出为含 %03d 的 PNG 序列）；what=frame 抽单帧（start 时刻，默认首帧）；what=subtitle 提取字幕流（streamIndex 默认 0）。

what.description: 提取内容：audio / frames / frame / subtitle（必填）。

tools.name: ffmpeg_frames
tools.description: 从视频批量抽帧为图片（PNG/JPG）。两种模式：every（固定秒间隔抽帧，如 every=2 表示每 2 秒一帧，默认 1）或 times（指定时间点列表，如 ["00:00:05","00:01:30"]，最多 20 个）。maxFrames 限制 every 模式的帧数上限（1-500，默认 100）。每次运行在 outputDir 下新建独立 run-* 子目录，只返回本次运行的输出目录、文件清单与数量，便于后续视觉模型读图。

times.description: 时间点列表（与 every 二选一，最多 20 个，秒数或 HH:MM:SS.mmm）。

maxFrames.description: every 模式帧数上限 1-500（默认 100）。

outputDir.description: 输出目录（可选，默认输入同目录 <文件名>-frames）；每次运行会在其中新建 run-* 独立子目录。

tools.description: Generates regional distribution maps, which are usually used to show the administrative divisions and coverage of a dataset. The name should be more specific and add attributive descriptions, for example, "西安市" is better than "西安", "杭州西湖区" is better than "西湖区". It cannot be a specific place name or a vague name, such as "其它".

style.description: Style settings.

fillColor.description: Fill color, rgb or rgba format.

colors.description: Data color list, in rgb or rgba format.

dataType.description: The type of the data value, numeric or enumeration type

dataValue.description: Data value, numeric string or enumeration string.

subdistricts.description: Sub-administrative regions are used to display the regional composition or regional distribution of related data.

name.description: Keywords for the Chinese name of an administrative region (must be within China), and must be one of China, province, city, district, or county. The name should be more specific and add attributive descriptions, for example, "西安市" is better than "西安", "杭州西湖区" is better than "西湖区". It cannot be a specific place name or a vague name, such as "其它".

There are usually two scenarios: one is to simply display the regional composition, only `fillColor` needs to be configured, and all administrative divisions are consistent, representing that all blocks are connected as one; the other is the regional data distribution scenario, first determine the `dataType`, `dataValueUnit` and `dataLabel` configurations, `dataValue` should be a meaningful value and consistent with the meaning of dataType, and then determine the style configuration. The `fillColor` configuration represents the default fill color for areas without data. Lower-level administrative divisions do not need `fillColor` configuration, and their fill colors are determined by the `colors` configuration (If `dataType` is "number", only one base color (warm color) is needed in the list to calculate the continuous data mapping color band; if `dataType` is "enum", the number of color values in the list is equal to the number of enumeration values (contrast colors)). If `subdistricts` has a value, `showAllSubdistricts` must be set to true. tools.name: mcp__officecli__officecli
tools.description:
Create, read, and modify Office documents (.docx, .xlsx, .pptx) by running officecli command lines.

Pass an officecli command line in `command` (string or pre-split argv array); it runs through the same CLI you'd use in a terminal. Verbs: create, view (modes: text|annotated|outline|stats|issues|html|svg|screenshot|forms), get, query, set, add, remove, move, swap, validate, batch, raw, help, load_skill. Add --json to get/query/validate/view-issues for structured output. Examples (CLI syntax): create deck.pptx · add deck.pptx /slide[1] --type shape --prop "text=Hi" · set report.docx /body/p[1] --prop bold=true · view deck.pptx screenshot --page 2 · query book.xlsx "cell[bold=true]". Discover verbs/flags with `help`, and an element's schema with `help <format> <element>` (e.g. help pptx shape).

Paths are 1-based: /slide[1]/shape[2], /body/p[3], /Sheet1/A1. Props are key=value strings.

Delivery gate (before reporting a document finished — any failure = fix and re-check, do NOT deliver; validate passing is NOT delivery, 'looks like a real document' is):
1. Schema: `validate <file>` -> clean, no errors.
2. Content: `view <file> issues` -> no overflow/format/structure issues; and scan `view <file> text` for leftover placeholders (xxxx, lorem/ipsum, <TODO>, {{...}}, $VAR$, empty ()/[]).
3. Visual audit: `view <file> screenshot --page N` renders the page/slide and returns it as an image shown to you (or --grid auto for a whole-doc contact sheet). Judge it adversarially (assume problems exist) for overlap, text overflow, off-slide shapes, dark-on-dark, misalignment; fix positions/sizes (`set <file> <path> --prop x=.. --prop y=..`) and re-screenshot until right; if the screenshot can't render, say 'not visually verified'. Whether this audit is mandatory is format-specific (slide decks need it most — absolute-positioned shapes overlap invisibly to text modes), so run `load_skill pptx` (or word / excel) for the authoritative gate. The per-format SKILL.md, not this blurb, is the source of truth for what 'done' requires.
4. Flush to disk: end with `save <file>` — this guarantees your edits are written to disk before you hand the file off. Required final step, not optional (always safe — never errors or loses work; `close` also flushes if you want to end the session too).

## Strategy
Use view (outline/stats/issues/annotated) to understand the document first, then get/query to inspect details, then set/add/remove to modify.
View modes: text, annotated, outline, stats, issues, html, svg (pptx only), screenshot, forms (docx only).
Before delivering, pass the delivery gate (see the tool description): validate clean, view issues clean, then a visual audit via view mode=screenshot when layout matters (slide decks most of all). Whether the visual audit is mandatory is format-specific — run `load_skill <pptx|word|excel>` for the authoritative per-format gate.
For 3+ mutations on the same file, use batch (one open/save cycle) instead of separate calls.
Get output keys can be used directly as Set input keys (round-trip safe).
Colors: FF0000, red, rgb(255,0,0), accent1. Sizes: 24pt. Positions: 2cm, 1in, 72pt, or raw EMU.
Paths are 1-based: /slide[1]/shape[2], /body/p[3], /Sheet1/A1.


IMPORTANT — before you create/add/set/remove on any Office file, FIRST run the command `load_skill <X>` for that file type (it loads the build guide and tells you to consult `help` for the schema). Pick X by need: pptx → slide decks / presentations · word → Word docs, reports, letters, memos · excel → spreadsheets, financial models, dashboards · morph-ppt → cross-slide Morph animation / continuous motion · morph-ppt-3d → 3D Morph decks (GLB models, camera) · pitch-deck → fundraising / investor decks (seed, Series A/B/C) · academic-paper → academic papers / research reports · data-dashboard → data dashboards · financial-model → financial models / projections · word-form → fillable forms, content controls, protected docs. (run `load_skill` with no name to list all skills.)

command.description: The officecli command line — either a single string (e.g. "add deck.pptx /slide[1] --type shape --prop text=Hi") or a pre-split argv array of strings (use the array form when an argument contains spaces or quotes). A leading 'officecli' is optional. Examples: "help" lists commands; "help pptx shape" shows an element's schema; "view deck.pptx text" reads it; "view deck.pptx screenshot --page 2" returns a rendered image; add --json to get/query/validate for structured output. Run help first to learn the verbs and flags.

tools.name: memory_register_document
tools.description: Register an agent-authored document (research report, design doc, long digest) into memory as a pointer row. Write-ownership split: the full text stays agent-owned on disk — the pipeline never reads or rewrites it; the DB stores only the summary + doc_path + evidence. Validates the file exists (absolute path, non-empty regular file), intersects evidence with real memory ids (all-fabricated evidence is rejected; unknown ids are dropped and the row is tagged evidence_degraded), and dedupes: re-registering the same path or title supersedes the old row (the old file is never touched; content_history stays traceable), while a merely near-duplicate summary of a different document row is rejected — update that row instead. On success the absorbed atomic evidence rows leave the active face in the same transaction (recoverable, nothing deleted); constraint/preference rows and other document/summary rows are never auto-archived, and keep_evidence_active: true opts out. Ids this same document absorbed on an earlier version still count as its evidence, so re-registering a new version is not read as fabricated evidence. Use for 'where is the conclusion doc for this project?' lookups; atomic facts still go to memory_save.

path.description: Absolute path of the document file (~ is expanded); must already exist as a non-empty regular file. The full text stays agent-owned — this pipeline never touches it.

title.description: Short unique title (English recommended: it is the cross-language stable dedupe/supersede key)

summary.description: One-paragraph summary stored in the DB and used for injection (any language)

importance.description: 1-5 (default 3); the summary row injects at the next-priority tier within documentInjectBudget when importance >= threshold

evidence.description: Memory ids this document is grounded in (atomic facts, not other pointer rows); each is verified against the store — fabricated evidence is rejected, unknown/archived ids are dropped and the row is tagged evidence_degraded, except ids this same document absorbed on an earlier version, which stay its evidence. On success the absorbed atomic rows leave the active face unless keep_evidence_active is true.

keep_evidence_active.description: Opt out of archiving the evidence rows absorbed by this document. Default false: after a successful registration the absorbed atomic rows leave the active face (recoverable, nothing deleted; constraint/preference rows and other document/summary rows are never auto-archived).

sensitivity.description: Optional sensitivity label (free-form, e.g. personal). Part of the supersede matching key — same path/title with a different sensitivity stays a separate document.

agent_scope.description: Optional explicit agent-scope declaration (issue #170): 'global' or '*' makes this document visible to every agent; any other value narrows it to that label. Overrides the automatic carrier label for this write; honored even when automatic scope labeling is disabled.

workspace_scope.description: Optional explicit workspace-scope declaration (issue #170): 'global' or '*' makes this document visible in every workspace; any other value narrows it to that label. Overrides the automatic carrier label for this write; honored even when automatic scope labeling is disabled.

tools.name: memory_runtime
tools.description: Inspect or provision the LOCAL inference runtime that dsh-mneme's local (offline) embedding and rerank need: the transformers + onnxruntime dependency closure, hundreds of MB unpacked. It is deliberately NOT a default dependency — mneme's core stays lightweight and local vectorization is opt-in — so this tool is the hook that makes the heavy capability available on demand. Use action=status first: it is read-only and reports whether the runtime is ready plus what provisioning would cost. action=provision tries, in order: (1) adopting an existing copy from this profile's node_modules (no network; hardlinked when on the same volume, so no extra disk), (2) a configured local .tgz directory, (3) downloading from the npm registry against a pinned manifest, verifying every tarball's sha512. Provisioning can transfer tens to hundreds of MB and take minutes: unless the user has already asked for local vectorization, tell them that cost before calling it. action=verify loads the runtime and runs one real inference (strictly offline, so the model must already be cached).

action.description: status = read-only; provision = fetch/adopt the runtime; verify = run one real inference

overwrite.description: provision only: replace an existing payload (use when repairing a broken one)

tools.name: memory_save
tools.description: Persist one memory entry for future sessions (user preferences, project state, decisions). Call this when the user states a durable preference, a project decision is made, or a lesson is learned. Merges into an existing entry of the same type when the title matches. Save only durable, cross-session value (a preference, a decision with its rationale, an engineering constraint, a pitfall with its root cause). Trivial single-turn work does not belong here, and when unsure, do not save. If a memory only holds for one workspace or one agent, declare workspace_scope / agent_scope; otherwise leave both out. An unscoped memory is visible everywhere; a scoped one is filtered or downranked outside its scope. If this session's context is about to be compacted, first save a continuity note with this same tool (type: project, title: one stable title for this line of work, e.g. "continuity: <topic>"): current_work (what you are doing now), next_step, and any open question. Keep it to those fields, and reuse that same title for later updates: the store merges rows of the same type + title (the merge appends to the note instead of replacing it), so a fresh title each time just leaves a trail of near-duplicate project rows.

type.description: preference=user profile; project=project knowledge/state; decision=key decision; history=conversation summary; rejected_solution=rejected/abandoned implementation approach; pitfall=debugging lesson (symptom+root cause+fix); constraint=engineering constraint

content.description: Memory body

sensitivity.description: Optional sensitivity label (free-form, e.g. personal). Same-title entries with different sensitivity stay separate instead of merging.

occurred_at.description: Optional ISO-8601 instant the remembered event happened (differs from write time). Invalid values are ignored.

agent_scope.description: Optional explicit agent-scope declaration (issue #170): 'global' or '*' makes this memory visible to every agent; any other value narrows it to that label. Overrides the automatic carrier label for this write; honored even when automatic scope labeling is disabled.

workspace_scope.description: Optional explicit workspace-scope declaration: 'global' or '*' makes this memory visible in every workspace; any other value narrows it to that label. Overrides the automatic carrier label for this write; honored even when automatic scope labeling is disabled.

tools.name: memory_search
tools.description: Search the cross-session memory store for past context (solved problems, user preferences, project decisions). IMPORTANT: relevant cross-session memories are already injected into your context every turn — only call this when the injected memory block does NOT contain what you need, or you need to look something specific up. Substring-matches title/content/tags, and augments results with semantic (vector) recall + optional rerank when an embeddings provider is configured. Returns matching entries with source and timestamps. Use this when the task depends on earlier decisions, preferences, or project history that is not already in context, or to look for a newer memory behind one that seems stale. Skip it for facts you can read directly from the repository.

query.description: Search text; substring match over title/content/tags

mode.description: auto (default) = keyword hits first + vector fill when enabled; keyword = text only; vector = semantic recall first (falls back to keyword); hybrid = vector leads, keyword fills remaining slots

semantic.description: Shorthand: enable semantic (vector) recall (same as mode=vector when true)

rerank.description: Run cross-encoder rerank over candidates when a local reranker is configured (default true)

occurred_from.description: Optional ISO date/timestamp lower bound on when the remembered event happened (occurred_at, falling back to created_at). Date-only values are inclusive from that day's 00:00Z.

occurred_to.description: Optional ISO date/timestamp upper bound on occurred_at. Date-only values are inclusive through that day's 23:59:59.999Z.

workspace_scope.description: Optional explicit workspace-scope correction: 'global' or '*' widens visibility to every workspace; any other value narrows it to that label. Omit to keep the current workspace scope. Recorded as an explicit scope decision (audited).

max_goal_rounds.description: Replacement cap; valid only with action edit.

blocked_reason.description: Required only with action blocked: the concrete condition that persisted across rounds and blocks progress.

tools.name: validate_dsh_ui
tools.description: Validate the JSON body of a ```dsh-ui fence BEFORE emitting it — use for non-trivial specs (≥3 nodes or containing a table); skip for trivial ones (≤2 nodes). Pass the exact JSON text you are about to put inside the fence as the "spec" argument (a string). Returns a [genui-validation] protocol block with status, diagnostics, next action, and reply_language=conversation. When invalid JSON is repairable, repaired_json contains the fixed body; emit it only with next=emit_repaired_fence. A warning=block_markdown requires the indicated replacement node and another validation call.

oneOf.description: The exact JSON text of the fence body.

spec.description: The dsh-ui fence body to validate: pass the JSON as a string for an exact check, or as the spec object.

tools.name: wait_agent
tools.description: Wait for the next teammate status, mailbox, or shared-task change after this call starts. This never wakes inactive members and returns noProgress immediately when no other member is running or provisioning. Re-list after wakeup or timeout instead of polling.

timeout_ms.description: Wait duration in milliseconds, from 10000 through 3600000. Defaults to 30000.

tools.name: web_fetch
tools.description: Fetch the content of a specific HTTP(S) URL and return it decoded to text.

url.description: The HTTP(S) URL to fetch.

tools.name: web_search
tools.description: Search the web for current information. Returns an optional summary answer and a list of source URLs.

queries.description: 1–4 search queries; their results are merged.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

meta.description: The workflow identity as plain JSON, not code.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact operation the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

[短期上下文] 最近对话（共 3 轮）：
Q: WorkBuddy有没有每天自动签到领积分的工具
A: 有的！而且**已经帮你在本机装好了，还当场跑通了** —— 这感觉就像：你以为要自己蹲点抢红包，结果我直接把闹钟定好了，红包自动进兜。😎

## 一、江湖上现成的三件兵器

| 兵器 | 路数 | 适配本机？ |
|---|---|---|
| [88lin/workbuddy-auto-signin](https://github.com/88lin/workbuddy-auto-signin) | 零依赖 Python 单文件 + 系统定时器，签到 + 成长中心全包 | ✅ **已装，已验证** |
| [dsh-buddy-checkin](https://github.com/corrinehu/dsh-buddy-checkin) | DSH 插件，启动时自动签到 | ⚠️ 不开 DSH 那天就漏签，且 `dsh` 命令本机没进 PATH |
| [WorkDaddy](https://github.com/babygoton/WorkDaddy) | CDP 注入桌面端套件（多账号/主题/自动化） | 太重，为签到杀鸡用牛刀 |

## 二、本机实测结果（不是吹牛，是日志）

```
凭据探测：~/.config/CodeBuddyExtension/Data/Public/auth/workbuddy-desktop.info  ✅ 明文格式
doctor：  AUTH_READY（本地凭据格式有效）
status：  今日已签 · 连续 3 天 · 今日 +100 · 累计 300 积分
auto：    Buddy 旅行中（咖啡馆，约 3 小时后回）· 领任务奖 +100 积分
```

## 三、定时任务已装进 crontab

```bash
# 每天 00:05 —— 签到 + 成长中心
5 0 * * * /usr/bin/python3 ...

Q: 改未每天 08:02 起自动领，
A: 改好了，08:02 准时开工。这就叫——**闹钟一响，积分自己长脚跑进兜里**。😎

## 改了什么

| 项 | 原来 | 现在 |
|---|---|---|
| 主签时间 | 00:05（半夜鸡叫） | **08:02**（人醒它也醒） |
| 补签兜底 | 01/05/09/13/17/21 点 | **12:02 / 16:02 / 20:02** |

兜底轮次特意挪到主签之后 —— 08:02 那次要是因为关机、断网、网络没睡醒跑砸了，后面三趟会先查状态、**没签就补**，连签链条不断。Buddy 出门旅行带回的礼物也能顺手领回来，不至于压到第二天。

## 现行 crontab（`crontab -l` 实拍）

```bash
# 每天 08:02 签到 + 成长中心（主签）
2 8 * * * /usr/bin/python3 .../signin.py silent >> .../cron.log 2>&1

# 补签兜底 + 成长中心轮询：12/16/20 点
2 12,16,20 * * * WORKBUDDY_SIGNIN_LOG=.../signin-poll.log /usr/bin/python3 .../signin.py silent-poll >> .../cron.log 2>&1
```

## 验证结果

- 模拟 cron 空环境（`env -i`）跑两条命令：**exit=0，双通过**
- cron 守护进程在跑：root 起的 `/usr/sbin/cron -f`，状态 active
- 日志末条：今日已签过 · 连续 3 天 · 累计 300 积分 · Buddy 咖啡馆旅行中

```dsh-ui
{"title":"签到时间表 · 已改 08:02","gap":12,"items":[{"type":"her

Q: 今天没签到，我手动签到的，啥情况
A: 用户报"今天没签到"，我来破案。先看现场——定时任务还在不在、cron 死没死、盘挂没挂。

[记忆库] 来自 dsh-mneme 的跨会话记忆（用户偏好与高优先级项目/决策）：
- [project] 插件 2.0.1 已装但需重启 dsh 才生效（重要性 5）：图片链路修复已合并到插件 2.0.1 并安装完成，但不重启 dsh 进程图片依然读不出来；今天 14 个问题里有 3 条（图片发送、图片显示、MD/HTML 预览依赖链路）都卡在这次重启上，是当前唯一未完成项。
- [decision] 修复方案：callId 缺失时自造 bridge-<uuid> 而非放弃（重要性 5）：在 /media/wangke/OFFICE/workspace/dsh-remote-bridge/src/host/dsh-0.2-bridge.ts 第714行改为 const callId = upstreamCallId ?? `bridge-${randomUUID()}`，只对「会话取不到」和「题目为空」两种情况 return delegate，callId 缺失不再放弃。构建后 lib 拷贝到 web 和 desktop 两个 profile 的 node_modules/dsh-remote-bridge。
- [decision] 插件通过npm发包并升版发布以修复问题（重要性 5）：选择A方案（npm发包），通过将修复内容升版本号（patch/minor/major）后npm publish到自有registry，让DSH自动更新覆盖旧版本，从而持久化修复效果，无需手动cp或写watcher脚本。

That's why cron silently failed — cron couldn't run the script, and the >> redirect would fail too (the log file couldn't be created since directory doesn't exist, so cron's output goes nowhere... actually cron would send mail, but no mail agent, so nothing).

Interesting: crontab still has the entry, cron daemon is active (started 10月11), but script dir doesn't exist.

Wait — the crontab also has other entries referencing /media/wangke/OFFICE/workspace/dsh-plugins-src/check-dvr-update.sh and DSH运维/壳巡检. Let me check if workspace itself exists. Maybe the whole workspace dir was moved/reorganized. Memory mentions "分类目录放置，多层嵌套目录限定最多3层" — maybe the user reorganized.

Also need to check: is the signin.py anywhere else? Let me search.

2. Find signin.py elsewhere
3. Re-deploy in a proper location (respecting the ≤3 level nesting rule), reinstall crontab
4. Also add failure notification so silent failures don't happen again — e.g., a wrapper that writes to a log in a stable location (~/.local/state or ~/.workbuddy? No, /tmp banned). Better: put script in ~/.local/share or in the workspace. But if workspace dirs get reorganized... Hmm. The safest is to put the script in the user's home, e.g. ~/.local/share/workbuddy-auto-signin/ (stable, not affected by workspace reorganization), and logs in ~/.local/state/ or ~/.cache. Given user preference for workspace, but reliability matters more; I'll put script + logs in a stable home location and tell them, or better — ask? No, the user wants it fixed. |---|---|---|
| crontab 条目 | ✅ 还在 | 三条任务的定义完好无损 |

| **脚本本体** | 💀 **没了** | `signin.py` 全盘搜不到，目录整个消失 |
| 连带损失 | 💀 **一片** | crontab 里另外两条任务（dvr 哨兵、壳巡检）的目标也一起人间蒸发 |

**这就是死因**：cron 每天 08:02 准时去敲门，敲的是一间**已经被拆掉的房子**。它很敬业地执行了，然后每一条都扑空，输出重定向到一个不存在的目录也直接失败——所以 cron.log 里连一行报错都没留下。房子没了，连「我失败了」都喊不出来。

用户手动签到是对的——那时候系统层面已经躺平了整整一天。

三个 cron 条目指向的三个目录**同时消失**，说明这不是签到脚本自己的问题，是 `/media/wangke/OFFICE/workspace/` 这个工作目录被整体清理过一轮。今天 20:07 还有人在往 `dsh-remote-bridge` 写东西，说明盘和目录本身是活的，是**其中若干个子目录被单独删掉了**。

这是个需要你亲自核实的**重大信号**——有东西在动你的工作区。我先把签到救活，清理的事得你查。

## 抢救方案：把家搬到拆不掉的地方

之前把脚本放在 `/media/wangke/OFFICE/workspace/` 是我判断失误——那是你的活跃工作区，随时可能被清理， cron 任务放那儿等于把闹钟绑在一辆可能被拖走的车上。现在改迁到 `~/.local/share/workbuddy-auto-signin/`，在你的家目录里，属于用户级数据领地，不占工作区、不会被误清。

A: 有的！而且**已经帮你在本机装好了，还当场跑通了** —— 这感觉就像：你以为要自己蹲点抢红包，结果我直接把闹钟定好了，红包自动进兜。😎

| [dsh-buddy-checkin](https://github.com/corrinehu/dsh-buddy-checkin) | DSH 插件，启动时自动签到 | ⚠️ 不开 DSH 那天就漏签，且 `dsh` 命令本机没进 PATH |
| [WorkDaddy](https://github.com/babygoton/WorkDaddy) | CDP 注入桌面端套件（多账号/主题/自动化） | 太重，为签到杀鸡用牛刀 |

## 二、本机实测结果（不是吹牛，是日志）

```

auto：    Buddy 旅行中（咖啡馆，约 3 小时后回）· 领任务奖 +100 积分
```

## 三、定时任务已装进 crontab

```bash
# 每天 00:05 —— 签到 + 成长中心
5 0 * * * /usr/bin/python3 ...

Q: 改未每天 08:02 起自动领，
A: 改好了，08:02 准时开工。这就叫——**闹钟一响，积分自己长脚跑进兜里**。😎

## 改了什么

| 项 | 原来 | 现在 |
|---|---|---|
| 主签时间 | 00:05（半夜鸡叫） | **08:02**（人醒它也醒） |
| 补签兜底 | 01/05/09/13/17/21 点 | **12:02 / 16:02 / 20:02** |

兜底轮次特意挪到主签之后 —— 08:02 那次要是因为关机、断网、网络没睡醒跑砸了，后面三趟会先查状态、**没签就补**，连签链条不断。Buddy 出门旅行带回的礼物也能顺手领回来，不至于压到第二天。

```bash
# 每天 08:02 签到 + 成长中心（主签）

```

content.text:
查明了。不是脚本坏了，不是 cron 死了——**是脚本的家被拆了**。

## 案情还原

| 环节 | 状态 |
|---|---|
| crontab 条目 | ✅ 还在，定义完好 |
| cron 守护进程 | ✅ 活着，`10月11`起的，状态 active |
| **脚本本体** | 💀 **全盘搜不到，目录整个蒸发** |
| 执行痕迹 | ❌ 08:02、12:02、16:02、20:02 一次没跑 |
| 连带损失 | 💀 crontab 里另外两条旧任务的目标目录**也一起消失** |

**死因**：cron 每天 08:02 准时去敲门，敲的是一间**已经被拆掉的房子**。它很敬业地执行了，然后扑空；输出要重定向进那个不存在的目录，也失败——所以 `cron.log` 里**连一行报错都没留下**。房子没了，连"我失败了"都喊不出来。这就是**静默失败**，最阴险的那种。

**连带后果**：从签到记录看，`2026-10-11` 断了一天（脚本用补登卡救回来了，**补登卡现在余 0 张，底牌打光了**），`2026-10-12` 就是你手动签的。目前连签 11 天、累计 1100 积分。

## 更大的信号（这事比签到严重）

三条 cron 任务指向的三个目录**同时消失**，说明这不是签到脚本自己的问题，是 `/media/wangke/OFFICE/workspace/` 被整体清理过一轮。那里面还有你的 `dsh-plugins-src`（vision-router 哨兵）和 `DSH运维/壳巡检`。**有东西在动你的工作区，建议你亲自查一下是谁、什么时候动的。**

## 已抢救：搬家到拆不掉的地方

之前把脚本放工作区是我判断失误——那地方随时可能被清理，等于把闹钟绑在一辆会被拖走的车上。现在迁到 `~/.local/share/workbuddy-auto-signin/`，用户级数据领地，不占工作区。

另外，GitHub 直连、fetch MCP、uos 下载全被墙，最后走 `ghproxy.net` 镜像拿到**新版脚本 87858 字节**（上游这 18 天更新过，反而因祸得福）。

```bash
# 每天 08:02 主签
2 8 * * * /usr/bin/python3 /home/wangke/.local/share/workbuddy-auto-signin/signin.py silent >> .../cron.log 2>&1
# 12/16/20 点兜底
2 12,16,20 * * * WORKBUDDY_SIGNIN_LOG=.../signin-poll.log /usr/bin/python3 .../signin.py silent-poll >> .../cron.log 2>&1
```

两条命令都过了 `env -i` 空环境实测，**exit=0**。明天 08:02 见真章。

```dsh-ui
{"title":"排障结论 · 脚本家被端了","gap":14,"items":[{"type":"callout","tone":"error","title":"死因：脚本目录被整体清理","content":"cron 活着、任务在、凭据也在，唯独 signin.py 连目录一起蒸发。cron 每天准时去敲一间已拆掉的房子，重定向到不存在的目录也失败——所以日志里一行报错都没留下。静默失败，连『我失败了』都喊不出来。"},{"type":"table","columns":["环节","状态","证据"],"rows":[["crontab 条目","✅ 还在","crontab -l 正常输出"],["cron 守护进程","✅ 活着","10月11启动的 /usr/sbin/cron -f"],["脚本本体","💀 没了","全盘 find 无 signin.py"],["今日执行痕迹","❌ 全无","08/12/16/20 点零运行"],["另两条旧任务","💀 同命","目标目录齐消失"]]},{"type":"steps","steps":[{"title":"已迁新家","desc":"~/.local/share/workbuddy-auto-signin/，不占工作区、不惧清理"},{"title":"已拿新版","desc":"ghproxy.net 镜像下载 87858 字节新版（直连全被墙）"},{"title":"已重装 crontab","desc":"08:02 主签 + 12/16/20 兜底，env -i 空环境实测 exit=0"},{"title":"当前战绩","desc":"连签 11 天，累计 1100 积分，今日已由你手动签过"}]},{"type":"callout","tone":"warning","title":"⚠️ 两件需要你决断的事","content":"① 补登卡已用光（余 0 张），以后再断签只能断，没底牌了——所以这次别再让它躺平；② crontab 里另两条失效旧任务（vision-router 哨兵、壳巡检）的目标目录也没了，我按规矩没擅自删，已备份待你去留，要删说一声。"}]}
```

> 这事的教训就一句：**别把定时任务绑在随时可能被清理的工作区**。现在它住进家目录了，稳。

tools.name: ask_user_question
tools.description: Ask the user a concise question when you need confirmation, a choice, or missing information before proceeding.

questions.description: Questions to ask the user before continuing.

id.description: Stable id for this question; echoed in the answer.

question.description: The specific question to ask the user.

header.description: Optional short heading for the question, such as "Confirm" or "Choose Mode".

options.description: Optional choices to show the user. If you recommend one, put it first and append "(Recommended)" to that label.

description.description: One sentence explaining the tradeoff or impact.

multi_select.description: Whether the user may select more than one option. Defaults to false.

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Managed `$DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. An unset variable expands to an empty string, so guard variables in such paths with `${VAR:?}`. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap; on expiry the command moves to the background as a job instead of being killed.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact command the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact command needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

tools.name: create_goal
tools.description: Create a persisted goal that keeps this session working across automatic continuation rounds. Use it when the direct human request is a long-running objective, even if the user did not say "goal"; not for single-turn work.

objective.description: The concrete completion objective inferred from the direct human request.

max_goal_rounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer limit on automatic continuation rounds.

tools.name: dsh_im_return_file
tools.description: Register a readable file or generated image for delivery through the current IM conversation after this turn. Requires an active IM delivery consumer; in Web, Desktop, or CLI conversations use the host present tool if available. Existing and newly created files are both valid. Success means queued, not sent; do not claim the user has received the file.

path.description: Absolute path, or a path relative to the current workspace.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

tools.name: ffmpeg_adjust

tools.name: ffmpeg_concat

tools.name: mcp__officecli__officecli
tools.description:
Create, read, and modify Office documents (.docx, .xlsx, .pptx) by running officecli command lines.

Pass an officecli command line in `command` (string or pre-split argv array); it runs through the same CLI you'd use in a terminal. Verbs: create, view (modes: text|annotated|outline|stats|issues|html|svg|screenshot|forms), get, query, set, add, remove, move, swap, validate, batch, raw, help, load_skill. Add --json to get/query/validate/view-issues for structured output. Examples (CLI syntax): create deck.pptx · add deck.pptx /slide[1] --type shape --prop "text=Hi" · set report.docx /body/p[1] --prop bold=true · view deck.pptx screenshot --page 2 · query book.xlsx "cell[bold=true]". Discover verbs/flags with `help`, and an element's schema with `help <format> <element>` (e.g. help pptx shape).

Paths are 1-based: /slide[1]/shape[2], /body/p[3], /Sheet1/A1. Props are key=value strings.

Delivery gate (before reporting a document finished — any failure = fix and re-check, do NOT deliver; validate passing is NOT delivery, 'looks like a real document' is):
1. Schema: `validate <file>` -> clean, no errors.
2. Content: `view <file> issues` -> no overflow/format/structure issues; and scan `view <file> text` for leftover placeholders (xxxx, lorem/ipsum, <TODO>, {{...}}, $VAR$, empty ()/[]).
3. Visual audit: `view <file> screenshot --page N` renders the page/slide and returns it as an image shown to you (or --grid auto for a whole-doc contact sheet). Judge it adversarially (assume problems exist) for overlap, text overflow, off-slide shapes, dark-on-dark, misalignment; fix positions/sizes (`set <file> <path> --prop x=.. --prop y=..`) and re-screenshot until right; if the screenshot can't render, say 'not visually verified'. Whether this audit is mandatory is format-specific (slide decks need it most — absolute-positioned shapes overlap invisibly to text modes), so run `load_skill pptx` (or word / excel) for the authoritative gate. The per-format SKILL.md, not this blurb, is the source of truth for what 'done' requires.
4. Flush to disk: end with `save <file>` — this guarantees your edits are written to disk before you hand the file off. Required final step, not optional (always safe — never errors or loses work; `close` also flushes if you want to end the session too).

## Strategy
Use view (outline/stats/issues/annotated) to understand the document first, then get/query to inspect details, then set/add/remove to modify.
View modes: text, annotated, outline, stats, issues, html, svg (pptx only), screenshot, forms (docx only).
Before delivering, pass the delivery gate (see the tool description): validate clean, view issues clean, then a visual audit via view mode=screenshot when layout matters (slide decks most of all). Whether the visual audit is mandatory is format-specific — run `load_skill <pptx|word|excel>` for the authoritative per-format gate.
For 3+ mutations on the same file, use batch (one open/save cycle) instead of separate calls.
Get output keys can be used directly as Set input keys (round-trip safe).
Colors: FF0000, red, rgb(255,0,0), accent1. Sizes: 24pt. Positions: 2cm, 1in, 72pt, or raw EMU.
Paths are 1-based: /slide[1]/shape[2], /body/p[3], /Sheet1/A1.


IMPORTANT — before you create/add/set/remove on any Office file, FIRST run the command `load_skill <X>` for that file type (it loads the build guide and tells you to consult `help` for the schema). Pick X by need: pptx → slide decks / presentations · word → Word docs, reports, letters, memos · excel → spreadsheets, financial models, dashboards · morph-ppt → cross-slide Morph animation / continuous motion · morph-ppt-3d → 3D Morph decks (GLB models, camera) · pitch-deck → fundraising / investor decks (seed, Series A/B/C) · academic-paper → academic papers / research reports · data-dashboard → data dashboards · financial-model → financial models / projections · word-form → fillable forms, content controls, protected docs. (run `load_skill` with no name to list all skills.)

command.description: The officecli command line — either a single string (e.g. "add deck.pptx /slide[1] --type shape --prop text=Hi") or a pre-split argv array of strings (use the array form when an argument contains spaces or quotes). A leading 'officecli' is optional. Examples: "help" lists commands; "help pptx shape" shows an element's schema; "view deck.pptx text" reads it; "view deck.pptx screenshot --page 2" returns a rendered image; add --json to get/query/validate for structured output. Run help first to learn the verbs and flags.

occurred_from.description: Optional ISO date/timestamp lower bound on when the remembered event happened (occurred_at, falling back to created_at). Date-only values are inclusive from that day's 00:00Z.

occurred_to.description: Optional ISO date/timestamp upper bound on occurred_at. Date-only values are inclusive through that day's 23:59:59.999Z.

tools.name: memory_register_document
tools.description: Register an agent-authored document (research report, design doc, long digest) into memory as a pointer row. Write-ownership split: the full text stays agent-owned on disk — the pipeline never reads or rewrites it; the DB stores only the summary + doc_path + evidence. Validates the file exists (absolute path, non-empty regular file), intersects evidence with real memory ids (all-fabricated evidence is rejected; unknown ids are dropped and the row is tagged evidence_degraded), and dedupes: re-registering the same path or title supersedes the old row (the old file is never touched; content_history stays traceable), while a merely near-duplicate summary of a different document row is rejected — update that row instead. On success the absorbed atomic evidence rows leave the active face in the same transaction (recoverable, nothing deleted); constraint/preference rows and other document/summary rows are never auto-archived, and keep_evidence_active: true opts out. Ids this same document absorbed on an earlier version still count as its evidence, so re-registering a new version is not read as fabricated evidence. Use for 'where is the conclusion doc for this project?' lookups; atomic facts still go to memory_save.

path.description: Absolute path of the document file (~ is expanded); must already exist as a non-empty regular file. The full text stays agent-owned — this pipeline never touches it.

title.description: Short unique title (English recommended: it is the cross-language stable dedupe/supersede key)

summary.description: One-paragraph summary stored in the DB and used for injection (any language)

importance.description: 1-5 (default 3); the summary row injects at the next-priority tier within documentInjectBudget when importance >= threshold

evidence.description: Memory ids this document is grounded in (atomic facts, not other pointer rows); each is verified against the store — fabricated evidence is rejected, unknown/archived ids are dropped and the row is tagged evidence_degraded, except ids this same document absorbed on an earlier version, which stay its evidence. On success the absorbed atomic rows leave the active face unless keep_evidence_active is true.

keep_evidence_active.description: Opt out of archiving the evidence rows absorbed by this document. Default false: after a successful registration the absorbed atomic rows leave the active face (recoverable, nothing deleted; constraint/preference rows and other document/summary rows are never auto-archived).

sensitivity.description: Optional sensitivity label (free-form, e.g. personal). Part of the supersede matching key — same path/title with a different sensitivity stays a separate document.

agent_scope.description: Optional explicit agent-scope declaration (issue #170): 'global' or '*' makes this document visible to every agent; any other value narrows it to that label. Overrides the automatic carrier label for this write; honored even when automatic scope labeling is disabled.

workspace_scope.description: Optional explicit workspace-scope declaration (issue #170): 'global' or '*' makes this document visible in every workspace; any other value narrows it to that label. Overrides the automatic carrier label for this write; honored even when automatic scope labeling is disabled.

tools.name: memory_runtime
tools.description: Inspect or provision the LOCAL inference runtime that dsh-mneme's local (offline) embedding and rerank need: the transformers + onnxruntime dependency closure, hundreds of MB unpacked. It is deliberately NOT a default dependency — mneme's core stays lightweight and local vectorization is opt-in — so this tool is the hook that makes the heavy capability available on demand. Use action=status first: it is read-only and reports whether the runtime is ready plus what provisioning would cost. action=provision tries, in order: (1) adopting an existing copy from this profile's node_modules (no network; hardlinked when on the same volume, so no extra disk), (2) a configured local .tgz directory, (3) downloading from the npm registry against a pinned manifest, verifying every tarball's sha512. Provisioning can transfer tens to hundreds of MB and take minutes: unless the user has already asked for local vectorization, tell them that cost before calling it. action=verify loads the runtime and runs one real inference (strictly offline, so the model must already be cached).

action.description: status = read-only; provision = fetch/adopt the runtime; verify = run one real inference

overwrite.description: provision only: replace an existing payload (use when repairing a broken one)

tools.name: memory_save
tools.description: Persist one memory entry for future sessions (user preferences, project state, decisions). Call this when the user states a durable preference, a project decision is made, or a lesson is learned. Merges into an existing entry of the same type when the title matches. Save only durable, cross-session value (a preference, a decision with its rationale, an engineering constraint, a pitfall with its root cause). Trivial single-turn work does not belong here, and when unsure, do not save. If a memory only holds for one workspace or one agent, declare workspace_scope / agent_scope; otherwise leave both out. An unscoped memory is visible everywhere; a scoped one is filtered or downranked outside its scope. If this session's context is about to be compacted, first save a continuity note with this same tool (type: project, title: one stable title for this line of work, e.g. "continuity: <topic>"): current_work (what you are doing now), next_step, and any open question. Keep it to those fields, and reuse that same title for later updates: the store merges rows of the same type + title (the merge appends to the note instead of replacing it), so a fresh title each time just leaves a trail of near-duplicate project rows.

type.description: preference=user profile; project=project knowledge/state; decision=key decision; history=conversation summary; rejected_solution=rejected/abandoned implementation approach; pitfall=debugging lesson (symptom+root cause+fix); constraint=engineering constraint

content.description: Memory body

sensitivity.description: Optional sensitivity label (free-form, e.g. personal). Same-title entries with different sensitivity stay separate instead of merging.

occurred_at.description: Optional ISO-8601 instant the remembered event happened (differs from write time). Invalid values are ignored.

agent_scope.description: Optional explicit agent-scope declaration (issue #170): 'global' or '*' makes this memory visible to every agent; any other value narrows it to that label. Overrides the automatic carrier label for this write; honored even when automatic scope labeling is disabled.

workspace_scope.description: Optional explicit workspace-scope declaration: 'global' or '*' makes this memory visible in every workspace; any other value narrows it to that label. Overrides the automatic carrier label for this write; honored even when automatic scope labeling is disabled.

tools.name: memory_search
tools.description: Search the cross-session memory store for past context (solved problems, user preferences, project decisions). IMPORTANT: relevant cross-session memories are already injected into your context every turn — only call this when the injected memory block does NOT contain what you need, or you need to look something specific up. Substring-matches title/content/tags, and augments results with semantic (vector) recall + optional rerank when an embeddings provider is configured. Returns matching entries with source and timestamps. Use this when the task depends on earlier decisions, preferences, or project history that is not already in context, or to look for a newer memory behind one that seems stale. Skip it for facts you can read directly from the repository.

query.description: Search text; substring match over title/content/tags

mode.description: auto (default) = keyword hits first + vector fill when enabled; keyword = text only; vector = semantic recall first (falls back to keyword); hybrid = vector leads, keyword fills remaining slots

semantic.description: Shorthand: enable semantic (vector) recall (same as mode=vector when true)

rerank.description: Run cross-encoder rerank over candidates when a local reranker is configured (default true)

occurred_from.description: Optional ISO date/timestamp lower bound on when the remembered event happened (occurred_at, falling back to created_at). Date-only values are inclusive from that day's 00:00Z.

occurred_to.description: Optional ISO date/timestamp upper bound on occurred_at. Date-only values are inclusive through that day's 23:59:59.999Z.

tools.name: memory_update
tools.description: Modify an existing memory entry (title, content, type, tags, importance).

reason.description: Optional context for the correction (what the user actually said/wanted), recorded for reflection

agent_scope.description: Optional explicit agent-scope correction (issue #170): 'global' or '*' widens visibility to every agent; any other value narrows it to that label. Omit to keep the current agent scope. Recorded as an explicit scope decision (audited).

workspace_scope.description: Optional explicit workspace-scope correction: 'global' or '*' widens visibility to every workspace; any other value narrows it to that label. Omit to keep the current workspace scope. Recorded as an explicit scope decision (audited).

tools.name: modlens_read_image
tools.description: Read an image through the modlens vision bridge. Use whenever a message references an image the current model cannot see: a local file path or an http(s) URL to a screenshot, photo, chart, diagram, or document scan. Returns structured evidence with every word transcribed (ocr.full_text), layout regions in reading order, semantics, and an uncertainty list. Quote the evidence instead of guessing. For the same image and focus, call this tool once and reuse its returned evidence instead of calling again. Evidence for a pasted image carries an `attachment-id:` line: to read that image again with a new focus, pass the id as path, and do not search the filesystem for the file. Requires a configured modlens engine (run `npx @liustack/modlens doctor` in a terminal to check).

path.description: Absolute local file path, http(s) URL, or the attachment-id (sha256:...) from pasted-image evidence

prompt.description: Optional extra focus for the reading (e.g. "focus on the axis labels")

tools.name: present
tools.description: Declare existing files as final deliverables for the user. Use it when the user needs a separate file, especially Office documents, spreadsheets, and slide decks; prefer your final response when that suffices. The user opens the current files; their contents are not copied.

files.description: Usually the 1-2 most important deliverables; at most 4 per call.

path.description: Path of an existing regular file. Relative paths use the Session working directory.

description.description: Brief description for the user.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

tools.name: read_image
tools.description: Read a PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF file and return the image itself. Large images are downscaled automatically; do not install image libraries or create thumbnails to inspect an image.

file_path.description: Path to the image file, resolved by the filesystem backend.

tools.name: read_mcp_resource
tools.description: Read an MCP resource by URI from the named server. Use a listed URI or an expanded resource template.

tools.name: schedule_create
tools.description: Create a reminder in the current session that delivers prompt when it becomes due. Supply exactly one timing parameter: after_seconds, at, every_seconds, daily, weekly, or cron. Local times that do not exist in the zone are skipped; repeated local times fire once, at the earlier instant. After downtime, a recurring reminder delivers only its latest missed occurrence. Delivery can repeat after a crash.

prompt.description: Reminder content to present when the target becomes due.

title.description: Task name of at most 120 characters, shown on the task card and in task lists.

every_seconds.description: Fixed-rate interval in whole seconds, at least 60, aligned to the creation time; changing it with schedule_update re-aligns it to the save time.

daily.description: Every day at a local time.

time.description: HH:mm:ss with optional 1-3 fractional digits, for example 23:00:00.

time_zone.description: UTC or IANA Area/Location, for example Asia/Shanghai.

weekly.description: On the given weekdays at a local time.

time.description: HH:mm:ss with optional 1-3 fractional digits, for example 09:00:00.

time_zone.description: UTC or IANA Area/Location, for example Asia/Shanghai.

weekdays.description: ISO weekdays, Monday 1 through Sunday 7, without repetitions.

cron.description: Five-field Vixie cron expression in a time zone.

expression.description: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week, for example "*/15 9-17 * * 1-5". When both day fields are restricted, a date matches if either one matches.

time_zone.description: UTC or IANA Area/Location, for example Asia/Shanghai.

at.description: Absolute target: an RFC 3339 date-time with offset, or a local date, time, and IANA time_zone.

tools.name: schedule_delete
tools.description: Delete a reminder in the current session, active or inactive. Deletion does not retract a reminder message that is already queued.

tools.name: schedule_list
tools.description: List the active reminders in the current session.

tools.name: schedule_update
tools.description: Change a reminder in place, keeping its id. Supply a new title, prompt, or at most one timing parameter; omitted fields keep their stored values. To change a relative delay, create a new reminder.

title.description: New task name of at most 120 characters.

every_seconds.description: Fixed-rate interval in whole seconds, at least 60, aligned to the creation time; changing it with schedule_update re-aligns it to the save time.

daily.description: Every day at a local time.

time.description: HH:mm:ss with optional 1-3 fractional digits, for example 23:00:00.

time_zone.description: UTC or IANA Area/Location, for example Asia/Shanghai.

weekly.description: On the given weekdays at a local time.

time.description: HH:mm:ss with optional 1-3 fractional digits, for example 09:00:00.

time_zone.description: UTC or IANA Area/Location, for example Asia/Shanghai.

weekdays.description: ISO weekdays, Monday 1 through Sunday 7, without repetitions.

cron.description: Five-field Vixie cron expression in a time zone.

expression.description: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week, for example "*/15 9-17 * * 1-5". When both day fields are restricted, a date matches if either one matches.

time_zone.description: UTC or IANA Area/Location, for example Asia/Shanghai.

at.description: Absolute target: an RFC 3339 date-time with offset, or a local date, time, and IANA time_zone.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send one durable message to another Team member. A running target receives it at the nearest step boundary; an inactive target starts or resumes a turn.

target.description: Member target returned by spawn_teammate or list_agents, including lead.

tools.name: skill
tools.description: Load the full instructions for a skill. Call it before acting on a task that names or clearly matches a skill in the session skill catalog.

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

tools.name: spawn_teammate
tools.description: Create one named, durable teammate. Only the Team Lead may call this tool.

description.description: Short description of the delegated responsibility.

prompt.description: Complete initial task for the teammate.

context.description: fresh starts without Lead history; fork inherits completed Lead turns. Defaults to fresh.

tools.name: subagent
tools.description: Delegate a self-contained task to a subagent (a separate agent that works in its own context) to offload focused, independent work — research, a scoped implementation, an analysis — so it does not consume this conversation's context. The subagent returns its result, not its intermediate steps. It runs in the background by default and returns a subagent id you can continue with `send_message`; you are notified when the run settles.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The complete, self-contained task for the subagent. It does not share this conversation's context, so include everything it needs.

run_in_background.description: Defaults to true. Set false only when your next action depends on the result.

tools.name: subagent_fork
tools.description: Delegate a task to a subagent that inherits this conversation: a child agent seeded with all completed turns so far (it does not see the current in-flight turn). Use this when the subtask builds on this conversation's context — a follow-up analysis, a review, a continuation — without consuming this conversation's context for the work itself. You receive its result, not its intermediate steps. It runs in the background by default and returns a subagent id you can continue with `send_message`; you are notified when the run settles.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The task for the subagent. It already sees this conversation's completed turns, so build on them freely and state only what is new.

run_in_background.description: Defaults to true. Set false only when your next action depends on the result.

tools.name: team_task_create
tools.description: Create one unowned pending task on the shared Team task board.

description.description: Complete task details and acceptance criteria.

blocked_by.description: Task ids that must complete first.

write_scopes.description: Advisory workspace-relative file or directory prefixes this task expects to modify.

tools.name: team_task_get
tools.description: Read the complete latest value of one shared task before changing or executing it.

tools.name: team_task_list
tools.description: List shared tasks, including readiness, owner, revision, blockers, and write-scope warnings.

owner.description: Optional member target from spawn_teammate or list_agents, matching ownerName; use unowned for tasks without an owner.

limit.description: Number of rows, 1 through 100. Defaults to 50.

tools.name: team_task_update
tools.description: Compare-and-set a shared task action using the latest revision from team_task_get or team_task_list.

expected_revision.description: Current task revision used as the CAS precondition.

description.description: Replacement details for edit.

write_scopes.description: Replacement advisory write scopes for edit.

owner.description: Member target from spawn_teammate or list_agents for Lead-only reassign; omit to unassign.

tools.name: todo_write
tools.description: Record and update a task list to plan multi-step work and show progress; skip it for trivial single-step tasks. Add one todo per concrete step before you start. While work remains, keep the todos being worked on `in_progress`, several only when work runs in parallel. Mark each todo `completed` as soon as it is done.

todos.description: The COMPLETE task list, replacing any previous list.

content.description: What the task is — a short imperative line.

tools.name: update_goal
tools.description: Update the current goal.

revision.description: Exact positive revision returned by get_goal.

action.description: edit, pause, and resume require a direct top-level human request. complete and blocked are also allowed during an automatic continuation of this goal; blocked is rejected before the configured minimum round count.

objective.description: Replacement objective; valid only with action edit.

max_goal_rounds.description: Replacement cap; valid only with action edit.

blocked_reason.description: Required only with action blocked: the concrete condition that persisted across rounds and blocks progress.

tools.name: wait_agent
tools.description: Wait for the next teammate status, mailbox, or shared-task change after this call starts. This never wakes inactive members and returns noProgress immediately when no other member is running or provisioning. Re-list after wakeup or timeout instead of polling.

timeout_ms.description: Wait duration in milliseconds, from 10000 through 3600000. Defaults to 30000.

tools.name: web_fetch
tools.description: Fetch the content of a specific HTTP(S) URL and return it decoded to text.

url.description: The HTTP(S) URL to fetch.

tools.name: web_search
tools.description: Search the web for current information. Returns an optional summary answer and a list of source URLs.

queries.description: 1–4 search queries; their results are merged.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

meta.description: The workflow identity as plain JSON, not code.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact operation the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

content.text: 今天为啥没签到，又是我手动签到的

You are an AI agent powered by DeepSeek Harness.

You are a coding agent powered by the glm-5.3-flash model.

[dsh-mneme memory] Read once; it applies to every turn of this session.
1. Precedence: the current instruction and the repository's actual state outrank any stored memory. When a memory contradicts either, check the instruction or the repository itself before relying on it — memory_search searches stored memories only, so it finds earlier context, never the present state. Never treat an old memory as current fact.
2. Recall on demand: call memory_search when the task depends on earlier decisions, user preferences, or project history that is not already in context. Do not search for facts you can read directly from the repository.
3. Write back sparingly: use memory_save for durable, cross-session value — a preference, a decision with its rationale, an engineering constraint, a pitfall with its root cause. Trivial single-turn work is not worth a memory.
4. When unsure, do nothing. Not acting is a valid outcome: a useless memory is paid for by every future session.
5. Prefer the reversible tools. memory_archive hides an entry from lists, search, injection and consolidation, and memory_forget suppresses it from injection, search results and lists — both are recoverable. memory_delete is permanent, so reach for it only when an entry is wrong or unwanted, not merely stale.

Agent Teams is available in this session, but create teammates only when the user explicitly asks to use Agent Teams or teammates.

The Team Lead and all teammates share the same working directory and filesystem. Edits are immediately visible to every member. Split write work into disjoint scopes, record expected write scopes on shared tasks, and use task dependencies when work must be ordered. Write-scope overlap is advisory, not a lock.

Prefer read/edit/write for file changes. If a file operation returns FS_STALE_VERSION, read the current file, rebase your intended change onto the new content, and retry. Bash, formatters, code generators, and scripts are not fully protected by the filesystem version guard; coordinate them explicitly and have the Lead review the final diff and run tests.

Use the target returned by spawn_teammate or list_agents for send_message and interrupt_agent, or as owner when assigning or filtering shared tasks. send_message steers a running target at its nearest step boundary and starts or resumes an inactive target. inactive means no turn is executing; it does not describe task completion, success, failure, or waiting for other agents. provisioning means member creation is in progress; failed means member creation failed. A delivered peer item starts with its stable message id and sender name. A successful send is already durable even when its result says queued; do not resend it. Shared-task workflow is list, get, claim with the current revision, perform the work, then complete. Task readiness never starts an owner. Before wait_agent, use list_agents and make sure another required member is running or provisioning; use send_message first when the required member is inactive. wait_agent observes only changes after that call starts, never wakes a member, and returns noProgress immediately when no other member can produce a change. Re-list after wakeup or timeout. The Lead must wait for required teammates before giving the final answer.

Tokens prefixed with @ are paths the user explicitly referenced. Relative paths resolve from the workspace root; absolute paths identify files or directories on the host. A trailing slash marks a directory: list it when its contents matter. Anything else is a file: use the read tool when its contents are needed, and do not claim to have inspected it before reading. @"..." quotes a path containing spaces.

Check the [exit code: N] marker on every bash result; investigate failures before moving on.

Use the read tool — not shell commands like cat — to inspect text files. Use offset and limit to continue reading large files.

Read an existing file before overwriting it with write (the default fs-observation-policy requires it) and prefer edit for targeted changes.

Read a file before editing it (the default fs-observation-policy requires it), unless you just created or edited it in this session.

Use the glob tool — not shell find — to discover files by path pattern.

Use the grep tool — not shell grep or rg — to search file contents. Use read on a matched file when you need surrounding context.
